svg.title: CHOSEN BRICK / HEAVYGRAM kill chain - Iranian Telegram-controlled implants against dissidents and journalists
svg.desc: Two-lane kill chain. Left lane, the victim: 1 a researched contact on WhatsApp, Telegram or Instagram impersonating a known person or technical support, 2 a lure file posing as Pictory, RunwayML, Norton, a Telegram authenticator, Flash Player, KeePass or an MRI scan result, 3 a dropper that unpacks a Python implant into ProgramData folders and into a look-alike directory C:\Windows with a trailing space, 4 persistence through HKCU Run values, mutexes and Microsoft Defender exclusions, 5 stage 2 Python implants controlled through the Telegram Bot API with one bot per victim, 6 collection of screen, microphone, Zoom calls, browser messaging data, email and Gmail OAuth tokens, 7 exfiltration to Telegram, Vultr Object Storage or StorjShare and, in one sample, wiping. Right lane, the operator and the public record: A the Iranian state operator, MOIS per the FBI, B the defender response of the NCSC, FBI and AIVD advisory, C the Vultr download and staging infrastructure, D the Telegram bot infrastructure, E the impact on victims including leaks and plots abroad, F the exfiltration buckets and proxy services. Critical stages are shown in red.
svg.text: CHOSEN BRICK / HEAVYGRAM: Iranian Telegram-C2 implants vs dissidents
Vendor: NCSC + FBI + AIVD - Date: 2026-09-15 - Cluster: Iranian state actors (MOIS per FBI) - Day 113
TARGET: DISSIDENT, ACTIVIST OR JOURNALIST (Windows)
OPERATOR AND PUBLIC RECORD (what is known)
Researched contact on a messaging app
WhatsApp, Telegram or Instagram; impersonates a known person
or technical support; offers IT services, builds rapport
Tries the work device first, then pushes to a personal one
T1589 T1566.003 Spearphishing via Service
FBI: activity since fall 2023; NCSC: since 2025
Lure file posing as software or a scan result
Pictory, RunwayML, Norton, Telegram, Flash Player, KeePass,
or MRI scan results; decoy shows while the implant installs
User runs the file; all documented victims use Windows
T1204.002 User Execution: Malicious File
Pictory_premium_ver9.0.4.exe
Dropper unpacks a Python implant
Folders under C:\ProgramData: SMQDServicePackages,
ssh-cache-default; payload also to C:\Windows<space>\SysWOW64
The look-alike directory has a space after Windows
T1036.005 PyInstaller bundle + rantom.txt
Sigma 01: Image contains 'C:\Windows \'
Persistence and defence evasion
HKCU Run values winappx, SMQDService, Default_SSH, MicDriver
Mutexes ytyjyujyu, noi672pp434awkc12f and two more
PowerShell Add-MpPreference excludes the staging folders
reg query HKCU\...\CurrentVersion\Run
Stage 2 implant takes orders from Telegram
Telegram Bot API: getUpdates, sendDocument, sendPhoto, getFile
Prefixes: @ shell, # built-in command, ** write to file
AES with HMAC; config.xml encrypted; one bot per victim
T1102.002 T1573 api.telegram.org
winappx.exe smqdservice.exe RuntimeSSH.exe
Collection: screen, audio, messages, mail, tokens
Screenshots, microphone and Zoom calls via MicDriver + Rar
Telegram and WhatsApp browser data, Outlook, Chrome passwords
MsCache.exe collects Gmail OAuth tokens with Selenium
removable drives and phones (MTP) also collected
Exfiltration, and wiping in at least one sample
Telegram, Vultr Object Storage or StorjShare carry the data
Newer variants hide Telegram behind HTTPS or SOCKS5 proxies
NCSC: wipe of the whole system seen in one sample
FBI technical analysis does not describe the wiper
A
Operator: Iranian state cyber actors
FBI: working for MOIS; NCSC and AIVD: Iranian state actors
Names: CHOSEN BRICK (NCSC) and HEAVYGRAM (FBI)
Targets in the UK, US and Netherlands, among others
confidence: high (state), MOIS per FBI only
no group alias or individual named
B
Joint advisory 2026-09-15
NCSC, FBI and AIVD; FBI technical update to FLASH-20260320-001
12 sample hashes, 4 mutexes, paths, Run keys, domains
Detection signatures are referenced but not attached
ic3.gov/CSA/2026/260915.pdf and 260915-2.pdf
TLP:CLEAR on the FBI update
C
Download and staging on Vultr Object Storage
sgp1.vultrobjects.com/downloads/pictory/ serves the lure
micbucket.ams1.vultrobjects.com stages MSCache.exe
and credentials.json; the service itself is legitimate
Suricata sids 6300001-6300004
Pictory_premium_ver9.0.4.exe sha256 e8b633dc...
D
Telegram bot infrastructure
api.telegram.org used over HTTP and HTTPS with a bot per victim
No bot token, ID or chat ID is published
A bot found on one host cannot be linked to other victims
Suricata sids 6300005-6300006 (hunting)
KQL k2: ProgramData binaries to Telegram
E
Impact on people, not only machines
Data from some victims appeared on pro-Iranian leak sites
NCSC: Iranian services plotted kidnap or lethal operations
abroad; surveillance supports transnational repression
NCSC: 'almost certainly' supports repression
free NCSC services for high-risk people
F
Exfiltration buckets and proxy services
vultrobjects.com, storjshare.io, backblazeb2.com for data
iproyal.com, lightningproxies.net for proxied Telegram
All legitimate: investigate the process, do not blanket block
Sigma 05: ProgramData binary to Telegram or storage
H1: egress by initiating process
Detection anchors: C:\Windows<space>\ directory, Run values, Defender exclusions, ProgramData binary to Telegram, 12 hashes
Rules in this folder: Sigma 01-05, KQL k1-k3, YARA chosen_brick_heavygram.yar (3 rules), Suricata sids 6300001-6300006, PEAK hunts H1-H3.
Names, folders and Run values may change per the advisory: hashes catch the 12 samples, the path and behaviour rules catch variants.
Telegram and the storage services are legitimate: pivot on the initiating process. The wiper is documented by the NCSC only.
